title: Vaccinated
html_source:
Smallpox in Ireland– an historical note with possible (and unwelcome) relevance for the future (Jan 07, 2014)
Frank Houghton Department of Geography, NUI, Maynooth and Department of Public Health, MWHB

The reports of the Registrar General give an indication of the logistics involved invaccination against smallpox. For example The Registrar General’s (1911) decennial supplement for the years 1901-1910 notes that 903,591 successful primary vaccinations were administered during this period. This of course is a miniscule amount compared to the number that would be needed to treat the whole population of Ireland, even if such quantities of the vaccine were available… One obvious feature of the decline in the percentage of primary vaccinations is its link with the decline in the threat posed by smallpox. However removing the threat of the disease requires total/near total vaccination.
